subject: POC success criteria & KPIs — follow-up from discovery call
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@atlas-payments.com>, Priya Singh <priya@atlas-payments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-25T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: POC success criteria & KPIs — follow-up from discovery call

Thanks again for taking the time today — really appreciate the context on Atlas Payments' fraud-detection pipeline and where model latency and cost are blockers for scaling. Per our call, I put together a concise POC plan and suggested success criteria so we can align on scope and what "success" looks like. Please review and flag anything you want adjusted.

Summary (what we heard)
- Goal: Replace current rule-based signal enrichment with a Redwood-powered scoring model that preserves throughput while improving precision and lowering per-request cost.
- Traffic: ~10k auth events/day (spiky), peak bursts ~100 req/s, average 10 req/s.
- Hard constraints: 95th pctl latency target and clear cost budget.

Proposed POC objectives and KPIs
1) Latency
  - Target: p95 <= 250 ms (server-side measured at Redwood edge, end-to-first-token and end-to-generation for scoring calls)
  - Baseline: we will capture current baseline during first 48 hours of POC for comparison
2) Throughput
  - Target sustained throughput: 100 req/s for 5-minute windows with <1% request error rate
3) Cost
  - Target: average cost/token <= $0.0006 for the production-quality model used in POC (final cost will depend on tokenization estimates we validate during setup)
4) Quality / Business metrics
  - Precision uplift on high-risk alerts: +10% relative vs baseline ruleset OR absolute precision >= 92% on labeled eval set
  - False positive rate (FPR) <= 3% on evaluation dataset
  - Manual review pass rate: >= 90% on 100 spot-checked examples

Evaluation plan & ownership
- Atlas provides: representative sample traffic replay + labeled eval set (min 2k labeled examples) and a short rubric for manual review (owner: Sanjay)
- Redwood provides: dedicated POC environment, instrumentation dashboard (p95 latency, throughput, cost/token, error rate), synthetic load harness, and weekly progress reports (owners: Marissa & Rishi)

Timeline (proposed)
- Week 0 (kickoff): sign SOW, final traffic/schema exchange (target week of Jul 2)
- Week 1: infra onboarding, baseline capture, model configuration
- Weeks 2-3: run replayed traffic + live sampling, iterate on prompts & quantization profile
- Week 4: final evaluation, joint review, decision on production rollout or extension

Next steps
- I'll attach a draft SOW and the perf KPI spreadsheet (attached). Please confirm: (1) aligned on the p95/throughput/cost targets above, (2) whether you want a 4-week POC vs a 6-week POC (we can do 4 weeks + optional 2-week extension), and (3) who will be the security contact to route SOC2 evidence/questionnaire to.

Attachments: 2028-06-25-redwood-poc-sow-draft.pdf, 2028-06-25-performance-kpis.xlsx

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick 15 min call if you prefer to iron out scope vs timeline in real-time.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@atlas-payments.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya@atlas-payments.com>
Date: 2028-06-26T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC success criteria & KPIs — follow-up from discovery call

Thanks Jordan — good summary and aligns with what we discussed. A couple quick questions and requests before we sign off:

1) Latency measurement: when you say "server-side measured at Redwood edge," can you confirm whether p95 includes network transit between our collector and your edge? We need "application-level" latency for SLA purposes (i.e., from our API gateway arrival to scoring response).

2) Cost/token: the $0.0006 estimate looks fine as a starting point — can you show sample calculations? Our average request is ~350 tokens (post-tokenization) but there are outliers up to 2k tokens for some diagnostic flows.

3) Security: we will need SOC2 Type II evidence and an updated security questionnaire before we can onboard the replay traffic into an environment that touches customer PII. Our security lead (cc'ed Priya) will route next steps.

4) Timeline: our team would prefer a 6-week POC to cover edge cases and run a longer baseline capture. Would Redwood be able to support a 6-week cadence? If not, we can do 4 weeks with a defined extension process.

Assuming the above is addressable, we're happy to move forward. I've shared this thread with our security and infra teams.

- Sanjay
Head of Risk Engineering | Atlas Payments
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@atlas-payments.com>, Priya Singh <priya@atlas-payments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-26T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC success criteria & KPIs — follow-up from discovery call

Appreciate the questions — quick clarifications below.

1) Latency definition: p95 will be measured server-side at the Redwood edge and reported as "arrival-to-first-response-byte" at our endpoint (this excludes last-mile internet variability on Atlas' side). If you need an "API-gateway-to-client" view we can collaborate on an end-to-end synthetic test, but for the SLA we're happy to provide the server-side numbers we control.

2) Cost math: example calculation attached (see performance-kpis.xlsx). Example: avg request 350 tokens * 2 (in+out) = 700 tokens/request; at $0.0006/token => ~$0.42 per request. For 2k-token outliers we recommend running as batch/async flows or applying a different routing rule during spikes — we can show cost delta during setup. We'll validate tokenization on your sample data during Week 1.

3) Security: we will share our SOC2 Type II report and a completed security questionnaire. Priya — expect an email from our Security team with the package by EOD tomorrow.

4) Timeline flexibility: we can do a 6-week POC. Our recommended default is 4 weeks to get to an initial evaluation, with optional 2-week extension for edge-case validation. If Atlas prefers 6 weeks up-front, we'll adjust the SOW accordingly; timeline in SOW will reflect the chosen cadence.

Action items
- Marissa: please attach SOW v0.1 and confirm kickoff availability for week of Jul 2.
- Rishi: we'll need a pre-built dashboard for p95/throughput/cost; can you own instrumentation and share link before kickoff?
- Sanjay/Priya: please confirm the labeled eval set availability and whether we should expect PII in the sample traffic (this changes environment controls).

I'll update the attached SOW to note the 6-week option and include the measurement definitions.

Best,
Jordan
